summary: Wave-40 delta verified: reschedule date-parsing (webhook), one-tap Confirm, and HTML5 calendar drag reschedule. Backend 5/5 tests PASS. Frontend Playwright: BDM dashboard renders 'bdm-reschedules' panel with 'Confirm <date>' buttons (data-testid confirm-resched-<id>); month calendar (dash-month-calendar, 31 cal-day-YYYY-MM-DD cells) drag verified — Anil Kapoor visit moved from 2026-08-22 → 2026-08-24 (11:10 preserved) via HTML5 dragstart/dragover/drop, POST /site-visits/{id}/reschedule fired and visit persisted.
critical_code_review_comments: WebhookController::parseWhen relies on bare Carbon::parse without a timezone hint — a customer typing '3pm' resolves in the server's UTC timezone (Asia/Kolkata offset lost). Consider parsing with app timezone (config('app.timezone')) so '3pm' → 15:00 IST, not 15:00 UTC (which is 20:30 IST — 5.5h off). Currently the annotated proposed_at will book the visit at the wrong wall-clock time for Indian users.

SiteVisitController::confirmReschedule silently returns ok=true even when meta.proposed_at is missing (no reschedule occurs, task is still completed). Consider 422 when proposed_at is absent to prevent accidental one-tap closures of unparsed requests.

SiteVisitController::confirmReschedule picks the latest site visit by scheduled_at without filtering out completed/cancelled visits — if a lead has an older completed visit dated later than the current active one (edge case: past reschedule cycles), the wrong visit could be moved. Filter to whereIn('status',['scheduled','confirmed','rescheduled']).
SalesDashboardController bdm.reschedule_requests query does not paginate — a burst of customer reschedule replies could balloon the payload; consider limit(50).

WebhookController::annotateReschedule updates task title even when parseWhen returns null (falls back to 'Reschedule <lead> — preferred: <text>'). This is fine, but the awaiting-reschedule branch already re-prompts when the reply is too short/emoji-only; a mid-length unparseable reply like 'anytime' will still overwrite the task title (informational).

rca of the issue: None — all pass. Test iteration notes: (1) login submit button has no type='submit' — resolved by clicking via accessible role. (2) frontend uses localStorage['crm_token'] (not 'token'/'auth_token') — corrected in JS eval. (3) HTML5 drag-and-drop cannot be reliably reproduced via Playwright's mouse.down/move/up on non-mouse-based drag handlers; dispatching synthetic DragEvents directly (with DataTransfer) exercises the exact dragstart/drop listeners the app registers.
